chapter: New York and the Himber years
title: Richard Himber, Georgia Gibbs, Stuart Allen and the Studebaker show
summary: Himber renamed performers, including Georgia Gibbs and Stuart Allen when Joey Nash refused to change his name; he also made magic tricks.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Richard Hymnlessed was in several businesses. This is the guy you're talking about.

He was a producer. He was a, he had a brain that was so fast that people hated him. He, he, there was a girl by the name of, I can't remember her first name, but he finally changed her to by the name of Georgia Gibbs. Really? He changed her name to Georgia Gibbs. It was, I can't remember her.
It was an awful name if I remember.

She had another name and she used to record under that name when she wasn't with such and such a band, a band that she was with. And she was with us and, and Himba had an, Himba had the knack of, of giving people names. Same as Stuart Allen, who was our lead singer. Stuart Allen, his name was Allen Ross. Jewish boy. And we were doing Studebaker. And there was a, there was a fellow by the name of Joey Nash, who was a very fine singer. Was with the Himba band. And when he got the, when he got the, when he got the Studebaker show, the, the agency didn't want Joey Nash. Because Nash was the big advertising against Studebaker. Of course. If you want to mention the name Nash. So I'd ask him to change his name. Stuart Baker. He said, the hell with you, my name is Joey Nash and that's the way it's going to stay. And then they fired him. Then they got, Stuart Allen, so his name was Allen Ross, so he changed his name to, they wanted him to say Studebaker.
Did you tell him about being in here at P. Long's band?
No, no. That's interesting. No, I wasn't talking about that.
About the Colgate hour? I'm going down to Harrison, the other, to the shoe shop guy. I see y'all got this all the way down.

So he, uh, so he got Stuart Allen. Stuart's dead too. He's dead, and Himba was dead for three days before. But you asked me about Himba if he had any other. He was in the, he was in the manufacturing business of magic tricks. I was talking to somebody the other day that knew that he had some of Himba's tricks. He had rings, finger rings, that were the most amazing thing in the world. They all come apart and you couldn't get them apart and you couldn't put them back together. Except if you move down. And it's the same thing with these rings that you, you have to put like this and put them apart and put them together. Yeah. But he was, he was in that. He was the one that invented the milk trick. Taking the milk and making a cornucopia of paper and pouring the milk into the, into the paper cornucopia and nothing goes in. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
